correctness.rationale: Jacobsthal--Ljunggren gives \(B_j\equiv B_{j-1}\pmod{p^{3j}}\), so \(B_r\) converges and already equals its limit modulo \(p^r\). LTE gives the analogous Teichmüller convergence for \(q^{p^r}\). Their difference therefore controls the congruence exactly. The first binomial lift is \(q\) modulo \(p^3\), which yields the two stated low-level Wieferich equivalences. The verifier independently checks 60 cases through \(r=4\) and selected lift valuations.

value.rationale: The theorem organizes every higher prime-power layer of a natural congruence into one p-adic invariant, proves an initial-segment law, and identifies the cubic layer as a higher-Wieferich condition.

final_claim: For distinct primes \(p\ge5\) and \(q\), the levels \(p^r\) satisfying \(\binom{q p^r}{p^r}\equiv q^{p^r}\pmod{p^r}\) form an initial segment: with \(\beta_{p,q}=\lim_r\binom{q p^r}{p^r}\) and Teichmüller lift \(\omega_p(q)\), level \(r\) works exactly when \(r\le v_p(\beta_{p,q}-\omega_p(q))\); the square and cube thresholds are the mod-\(p^2\) and mod-\(p^3\) Wieferich conditions.
limitations: No closed formula or finiteness theorem for the p-adic distance.
